title: Netherlands's Quantum Strategy Sets 2035 Goals, Links Industry Growth to Cybersecurity
key_facts: Cabinet-approved Dutch quantum strategy submitted to parliament by Minister Heleen Herbert and State Secretary Willemijn Aerdts
Goal for 2035: technological leadership, less dependence on suppliers outside the EU, and resilience against quantum security threats
Builds on 614.9 million euros already given to Quantum Delta NL through the National Growth Fund
Not a new fully funded programme: actions are underway or within existing budgets, and ambitions will be adjusted if money is short

Government organisations to set cryptography policy by end 2026, have draft migration plans by end 2027, and finish high-risk migration to post-quantum cryptography by end 2030, medium-risk by end 2035
Strategy uses a possible 2029-to-2035 window for a code-breaking quantum computer and admits timing is uncertain
Says a fully independent Dutch supply chain is practically impossible; buying a quantum computer is an option to assess, not a contract
quote_evidence: The strategy does not establish a new, fully funded spending program for all its ambitions.
The strategy uses a possible 2029-to-2035 window for the arrival of such a computer while explicitly acknowledging that the timing remains uncertain.
why_it_matters_hint: A government timetable to replace vulnerable encryption, paired with industry goals that lack new funding.
notes: Official strategy as described by The Quantum Insider.
